findings.claim: Attributes already on T are ignored. Without a surrogate, the collector always takes the contractless path: every public read-write member is serialized under its name. It never checks T for [DataContract]/[DataMember], [MessagePackObject]/[Key], or [IgnoreMember]. The requirement says contractless applies only when T has no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject], and that attributes T does carry are honoured. A [DataContract] type from a dependency-free library is therefore serialized with the wrong keys and membership. The XML doc and README also describe this as always contractless, which contradicts the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonorsTypeAttributesTests.DataContractMemberNamesAreHonored. ProjectA.MyType is [DataContract] with [DataMember(Name="id")] and [DataMember(Name="name")] plus an unmarked Extra property. On head the JSON has keys Extra/Id/Name instead of id/name only.

findings.claim: The 'contractless' mode ignores the opt-out attributes that MessagePack's contractless behaviour honours ([IgnoreDataMember] / [IgnoreMember]). CreateContractlessMembers filters only on accessibility and writability. A public member that T explicitly excludes is still serialized, which differs from the contractless behaviour the requirement asks for.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonorsTypeAttributesTests.IgnoreDataMemberIsHonoredInContractlessMode. ProjectA.MyType has [IgnoreDataMember] public string Secret. On head the JSON contains "Secret".
